clusters.state_of_play: The Iran war's economic fallout has deepened further as Saudi Arabia shut down its critical 1,200-km East-West pipeline -- which carries 5% of world oil supply and has served for six months as the main alternative export route while the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut -- after a drone attack launched from Iraqi territory. Iraq's government confirmed the attack originated from its soil; Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed a commander and ordered an investigation into the operations command in Maysan province, bordering Iran, and Iraq shut three border crossings to Iran, while pledging not to retaliate. Saudi Arabia said it too would not retaliate but wants Iraq to take necessary measures; Iraq is reportedly under US pressure to rein in Iran-backed militias. Saudi Arabia is now seeking to boost oil tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz itself to offset the pipeline's loss, even as Iran and Oman have postponed talks on control of the strait, further straining energy markets. Australia's Energy Minister Chris Bowen is traveling to Saudi Arabia to shore up fuel supply amid the squeeze. Trump said he believes Iran was probably behind the pipeline attack, while separately predicting the Iran war will end soon after the mid-term elections and that oil prices will then fall sharply. This compounds the crisis triggered by the Houthi rebels' rapid seizure of Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline, including the port of Mocha and the strategic Perim (Mayun) island commanding the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the claiming of Zuqar island, and attacks on the Hanish islands -- more than 1,000 people have been killed or wounded and tens of thousands displaced in the fighting. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree declared Red Sea shipping safe for all vessels except Saudi ships. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has personally pressed Trump to launch direct military action against the Houthis as the advance threatens Yemen's fragile truce and Saudi Arabia itself. With both Bab el-Mandeb and now an alternative Saudi pipeline route imperiled alongside fears for the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices remain elevated but retreated Friday on hopes of renewed negotiations after notching sharp weekly gains, borrowing costs are rising, global markets are rattled including a six-week low on Australia's ASX, US gas prices remain at record highs, and Trump's Iran deal push is further complicated. Reports indicate Vice President Vance and Secretary Rubio have privately confronted Trump over his worst fears about the war's trajectory.
